http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24839v1.summary: Kaer is a multi-agent framework that protects the orchestrator's replanning step from malicious agent feedback, using abstract failure templates and restricted repair operators; it is evaluated on the new Cintra benchmark against Magentic-One and ControlValve.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24839v1.title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25855v1.summary: HabitusMem is a trained memory writer that stores a personalized LLM agent's beliefs about a user's evolving preferences, each with evidence, scope, and status, and reports top results on PersonaMem-v2 and VitaBench 2.0.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25855v1.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25898v1.summary: A critical review of clinical LLM reliability that covers hallucination, agentic error cascades, process reward modeling, and neuro-symbolic grounding, and argues that certification should audit reasoning steps as well as accuracy.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25898v1.title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26275v1.summary: dLoop restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a looped architecture that reapplies a shared block before token commitment, reporting top or tied-top accuracy on GSM8K, MATH, MBPP and HumanEval.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26275v1.title: dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26358v1.summary: A technical report introducing Beam, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters for coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks, with a 1M-token context window and a large-scale asynchronous RL post-training run.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26358v1.title: Beam Model Technical Report

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.summary: Seer is an inference-time framework that guides small local deep-research agents by using offline-trained tool-response and value models, raising GAIA accuracy for Qwen3.5-4B and 9B models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26531v1.summary: An arXiv paper presents an agentic system where LLM agents and deterministic tools optimize ranking-model features across a fleet under cost and QPS limits, improving normalized entropy by 0.31% on average.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26531v1.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26569v1.summary: Introduces EditSafetyBench, a 5,940-pair image-instruction benchmark, and finds that Gemini, GPT, and Qwen refuse far more unsafe text prompts than unsafe images paired with neutral instructions.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26569v1.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26613v1.summary: Presents AgentRoboCritic, a framework that analyzes frontier multimodal agents' robot control at the action level across 12 manipulation benchmarks, and releases a 12,844-action annotated dataset and a fine-tuned open-source critic.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26613v1.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26619v1.summary: TideCache is a serving system for hybrid LLMs on CPU-GPU superchips that reallocates GPU memory among cache types and streams KV prefixes layer by layer, implemented in SGLang and tested on GB300 and GH200.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26619v1.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26624v1.summary: PlayCraft is an automated framework in which a vision-based agent plays a game, reports its experience, and a crafter agent revises the game for mastery, yielding larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes than initial games in most cases.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26624v1.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26776v1.summary: Compares three ways of passing observations from perception agents to a language-model reasoner for flagging violent video, finding flat text matches a single audio-visual model (F1 0.967 vs 0.968) on XD-Violence.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26776v1.title: What Helps Language-Model Agents Review Violent Video? A Controlled Comparison with a Human Evidence Reference

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26863v1.summary: A study finds that when post-training on knowledge tasks with reasoning-style RL, models memorize hallucinations they generated, recalling reinforced ones 4.83% more on average than unrewarded ones (0.17%).
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26863v1.title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26966v1.summary: Presents the OPCP runtime, which mediates tool calls for AI agents and records uncertain supplier outcomes; tests use scripted requests and synthetic suppliers, with no language model evaluated.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26966v1.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26972v1.summary: Introduces TheaterBench, a benchmark of counter-intuitive video scenarios that violate physical laws or common sense, used to test how multimodal video models fail when visual evidence conflicts with their priors.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26972v1.title: When Perception Collides with Priors: Diagnosing Modal Polarization in Video Understanding Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26988v1.summary: Proposes a system that converts letter-of-credit bill of lading and invoice requirements into executable checks run by a deterministic verifier, reporting 82% correct verification on 345 real cases against 54% for a tool-using agent.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26988v1.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27068v1.summary: DM-PRM uses a general-purpose yes/no decision model to score each step zero-shot, without step labels or fine-tuning, and adds those scores to policy-gradient advantages, improving GRPO on ALFWorld and WebShop.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27068v1.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27084v1.summary: An arXiv paper audits the training-free kNNGuard prompt guardrail, finding its AUROC falls to about 0.55 on inputs over 1000 tokens, and tests length-routed banks, a long-context embedding model, and strided window pooling as fixes.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27084v1.title: Auditing and Adapting kNNGuard for Long-Context Prompts

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27090v1.summary: Across 50 agent systems, public reports show recovery mechanisms used often but rarely fully successful: of 128 real-use reports, 19 describe full recovery, 54 partial and 45 failed.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27090v1.title: Exercised, Rarely Recovered: What Public Reports Say About Recovery in 50 AI Agent Harnesses and Runtimes

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27092v1.summary: PLoQ is a 4-bit activation quantization method for LLMs that estimates a low-rank basis per prompt during prefill, quantizes those dominant components separately, and restores them in the GEMM without changing the weights.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27092v1.title: PLoQ: A Prompt-Specific Low-Rank Basis for 4-bit Quantization of LLM Activations

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27095v1.summary: epistemic-guard v0.5.2 is an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy that checks agent prose against tool receipts, gates memory writes by provenance, and runs on CPU without GPU VRAM.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27095v1.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27106v1.summary: Introduces a benchmark protocol and public artifact for LLM business workflows across six Python implementations, reporting that schema validity and task quality diverge, with PydanticAI, LangGraph, and DSPy scoring highest.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27106v1.title: Schema-Validated LLM Workflows: A Benchmark Protocol and Comparative Evaluation Across Six Python Implementations

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27119v1.summary: CTRL is a system that runs an RL learner and a persistent rollout engine on every GPU under CUDA MPS, reporting 1.11-2.24× the throughput of verl's asynchronous baselines across 24 Qwen3 workload settings.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27119v1.title: CTRL: Concurrent Training and Rollout for LLM Reinforcement Learning via GPU Co-Residency

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27124v1.summary: Proposes a round-trip check for latent world model planning that executes plans each CEM iteration and penalizes action mismatches, raising success on DINO-WM, LeWM and JEPA-WM at 0.2% to 3.1% extra planning time.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27124v1.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.summary: Introduces RI-Bench, a benchmark measuring whether senior LLM agents uphold their duties toward subordinate reports across peer review, appellate, and parliamentary settings, finding frequent deference to generic reviews and dropped witness limitations.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27154v1.summary: Measures how repetitive full repository histories are for code model training, finding typical repos hold about 19 copies of their current code and that near-duplicate deduplication across versions cuts this to about two.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27154v1.title: Git History Is a Pangenome: Repetition in Code Training Corpora and What Deduplication Removes, Keeps and Misses

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27155v1.summary: Finds that 4-bit quantization of reward models and LLM judges flips 1.1-12.3% of RewardBench preference decisions even when benchmark accuracy barely changes, and that these flips alter best-of-64 selections far more often than final answers.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27155v1.title: The Vulnerability Window: Decision Instability in Quantized Reward Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27216v1.summary: Reports a failure in which an on-device agent's earlier correct release of an item makes it more likely to wrongly release a still-restricted item, tested across 13 open-weight models, with a LoRA-based fix proposed.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27216v1.title: Correct Precedents Induce Policy Violations in On-Device LLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27294v1.summary: HookEvo uses an agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses, reporting 95.41% on ALFWorld and 70.56% on DBBench with a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, and releasing code.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27294v1.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27301v1.summary: Tracks 6,503 clinical cases across six HPO releases (Oct 2021–June 2026) and finds diagnostic rankers' accuracy jumps when a case's source publication enters HPO, then collapses when those links are removed.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27301v1.title: Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27306v1.summary: γ-Scape is a simulation and benchmark platform where agents compose motion tools and learned skills to complete mobile manipulation tasks in a persistent physical world, with tools for task evaluation and demonstration collection.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27306v1.title: $γ$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27326v1.summary: The paper proposes concept-normalized multilingual scratchpads and reversible model-adaptive reasoning codes to cut the token count, and so the inference cost, of chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27326v1.title: Reasoning in Fewer Tokens: Concept-Normalized Multilingual Scratchpads and Reversible Model-Adaptive Reasoning Codes

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27344v1.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27350v1.summary: Introduces GRACE, a 4,028-question GraphRAG benchmark built from LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata with four controlled evidence interventions, and proposes QCFSE-SA, which raises controlled-state accuracy from 57.17% to 62.78%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27350v1.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27376v1.summary: Proposes CSPD, which freezes the pre-RL model, distills each RL expert into a soft prompt, and composes them by concatenation; it matches multi-teacher distillation (67.83 vs. 67.79) with less serving overhead.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27376v1.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27443v1.summary: Introduces ADAPT, a post-training recipe that teaches a small language model when to request advice from a stronger advisor model, reporting higher success rates on TextWorld, LiveCodeBench and GAIA with about 1 to 2 advisor calls per task.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27443v1.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27494v1.summary: Typhoon OCR 2 is a Thai-focused OCR model in 2B and 0.8B sizes that handles prompt-driven field extraction and full-page parsing in one model, scoring 80.7 on Thai MDPBench versus 68.9 for version 1.5.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27494v1.title: Typhoon OCR 2: From Thai Document Transcription to Multilingual, Multi-Task OCR

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27504v1.summary: Extracting the assistant persona direction in 31 languages for Qwen3-32B finds these activation-space axes differ from the English one, with cosine similarity ranging from 0.378 to 0.911 and tracking language resource level.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27504v1.title: The Assistant Persona Differs Across Languages in Activation Space

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27521v1.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27536v1.summary: Introduces Open CDLM, a benchmark and open-source library for evaluating continuous diffusion language models, using Kernel Text Discrepancy and diversity diagnostics, and shows that conventional generation scores can be inflated by collapsed outputs.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27536v1.title: Open CDLM: A Benchmark and Library for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27607v1.summary: Introduces Tasklets, a set of small synthetic tasks testing recall, sequence manipulation, and state tracking, and uses them to compare many language model sequence-mixing layer types in controlled small-model experiments.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27607v1.title: Tasklets: A Unit-Test Benchmark for Language Model Architectures

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27618v1.summary: Proposes agent states as intermediate variables and a statistical-physics framework with a partition function to track a global potential in LLM agent reasoning during post-training, tested on two Qwen3.5-9B tasks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27618v1.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27645v1.summary: Proposes LS-MBPO, a lightweight residual reinforcement learning framework that uses latent world models instead of large image or video generators to improve pretrained vision-language-action robot policies, tested on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real ALOHA robot.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27645v1.title: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Subchunk Rollouts in Latent World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27652v1.summary: Studies post-training machine unlearning in the diffusion language model LLaDA-8B-Instruct, using WMDP as the forget benchmark and sparse autoencoders to compare static and stage-adaptive feature suppression across denoising steps.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27652v1.title: Auditing Post-Training Unlearning in Diffusion Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27656v1.summary: Proposes LeDAS, a dynamic data selection framework that scores training samples by hardness, learning progress and deterioration tracked via loss EMAs, reporting results matching full-dataset training at 50% selection on ImageNet-1K and LLM fine-tuning.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27656v1.title: Beyond Sample Hardness: Adaptive Data Selection through Learning Dynamics

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27673v1.summary: Hy-MT3 is a third-generation multilingual translation model family in 1.8B, 7B and 30B-A3B sizes, expanding language coverage from 38 to 102 languages.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27673v1.title: Hy-MT3: More Accurate, Robust and Practical Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27710v1.summary: CRAFT is an offline method that abstracts problem-specific details into slots, compresses shared expression templates once, and applies the edits to build shorter chain-of-thought training targets, cutting compressor budget by a median 90.7%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27710v1.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27712v1.summary: Proposes PreVIR, a lightweight text-only router that decides from the source sentence alone whether to invoke visual features in English-to-Chinese machine translation, reducing visual calls while keeping quality near always-on multimodal inference.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27712v1.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27721v1.summary: Compares three decision models and two LLMs in zero-shot use against fine-tuned multilingual encoders for four-emotion classification across 10 social-media datasets in five languages.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27721v1.title: Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27722v1.summary: Evaluates language models on seven scientific argumentation tasks (argument mining, rebuttal generation, discourse reasoning) using research papers, peer reviews, and grant proposals, and proposes a training framework that scaffolds argumentative reasoning.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27722v1.title: Beyond Math, Code, and Logic: Do Reasoning Models Transfer to Scientific Argumentation?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27734v1.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27738v1.summary: AVERT is a method that lets each token in an LLM request execute a variable number of Transformer layers so the request's mean depth matches a continuous budget, reporting 206 of 234 best-or-tied results across three LLaMA models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27738v1.title: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27741v1.summary: Introduces PlayScriptBench, a benchmark testing whether vision-language models can write executable game-playing programs, evaluated on 16 games across 4 genres, where even strong models perform poorly.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27741v1.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27750v1.summary: Introduces RoSci-Bench, a 1,220-sample diagnostic benchmark testing science vision-language models on information errors and losses, and RoSci-Agent, a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline that outperforms standalone VLMs on an Overall Robustness Score.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27750v1.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27759v1.title: DPMA: Learning to Compress Mixture-of-Experts Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27780v1.summary: Search-RSI is a self-improvement framework for multimodal search agents that expands the retrieval world with new tasks and evidence, reporting 9.8 and 9.5 point average accuracy gains at 9B and 27B across nine benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27780v1.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27784v1.summary: Neural Defend presents ARCAS 290M, a single frozen detector for AI-generated audio that it reports ranks first on the Podonos leaderboard and beats commercial and published detectors on ten public benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27784v1.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27807v1.summary: Evaluates zero-shot multilingual aspect-based sentiment triplet extraction across 12 languages, three domains and seven open-weight LLMs under four prompting strategies, finding direct monolithic prompting performs best.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27807v1.title: Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Zero-Shot Multilingual Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27808v1.summary: Proposes DistP, a theoretical framework extending zero-shot hyperparameter transfer from data-parallel training to local-update methods, reporting 8.1% lower validation loss and 10% higher downstream accuracy at 823M parameters without retuning.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27808v1.title: $\mathtt{DistP}$: Scaling Local-Update Training with Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27811v1.summary: Proposes shallow neural networks alternating simple-cell-like and complex-cell-like layers that give low confidence on unknown and adversarial inputs and remain competitive on standard classification benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27811v1.title: Redesigning Neural Networks to Not be Confidently Wrong even to Strong Adversarial Attacks

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27823v1.summary: Proposes MoLR, an adaptive recursion method for LoRA that recursively refines each token's down-projected latent with a shared transformation, using a threshold router to set depth, and reports gains over LoRA variants with negligible extra parameters.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27823v1.title: Mixture of Latent Recursions for Low-Rank Adaptation

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27831v1.title: DistDNA: Language Model Fingerprinting under Stochastic Decoding

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27839v1.summary: Introduces a multi-agent framework for verifying research claims that uses asymmetric Advocate, Skeptic and Arbitrator roles and a Belief-Delta stopping rule, reporting 2.4x fewer LLM calls across 200 runs on 40 hypotheses with DeepSeek-R1-32B.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27839v1.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27855v1.title: Anchors That Move Without Collapsing: Exclusive-Region Anchor Routing for Vision Transformers

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27865v1.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27870v1.summary: An arXiv paper comparing categorical (token-based) and continuous (flow-matching) prediction for visual world models in controlled 2D and 3D environments, finding categorical models more valid and compute-efficient.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27870v1.title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27891v1.summary: Introduces DICE, a speculative decoding method that pre-samples verification randomness and uses it with an existing drafter to direct drafting toward likely continuations, reporting throughput gains of up to 24.6pp over baselines.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27891v1.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27899v1.summary: Describes a two-tier industrial framework for automated UX attribution in web search: a fine-tuned Gemini XS telemetry model for macro sentiment regression detection, and a Gemini 3.0 Pro multimodal model for layout-level diagnostics.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27899v1.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27910v1.summary: Proposes interpretable embeddings built from yes/no/not-stated answers to natural-language questions, reporting that they match dense retrieval for entity matching on public product benchmarks while giving exact per-question explanations.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27910v1.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27913v1.summary: Introduces Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ), an evaluation framework that separates clean, merged, and split instance matches in a star forest so each failure mode can be weighted individually when reference instances are biased.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27913v1.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27915v1.summary: Introduces StereoVLM, a binocular vision-language model trained hierarchically on calibrated stereo images, reporting 95.17% depth accuracy and a 66.98 object-level score on its new Stereo3D-Bench.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27915v1.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27919v1.summary: The paper proposes Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), reward-independent representations derived from an action-centered canonical dependence matrix, and reports finite-state and zero-shot evaluations on discrete and continuous-control tasks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27919v1.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27951v1.summary: Introduces Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT), a linear-size attention method using sparsemax or thresholded ReLU gating, annealed Sinkhorn scaling and custom Triton kernels, reporting 97.40% zero-shot recall at L=262,144 on an NVIDIA L4.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27951v1.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27962v1.summary: Introduces Model Carving, which uses learnable scalar gates on each sublayer to learn Transformer weights and architecture together in one run, reporting lower validation loss than dense models at equal compute.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27962v1.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27963v1.summary: Introduces NoPeBench and NoPeWorld, which trains a small head on frozen diffusion transformer hidden states to flag and replace penetrating actions, cutting the average violation rate across six models from 74% to 16%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27963v1.title: Non-penetrating World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27973v1.summary: MemOnce proposes an LLM architecture that caches compact final-layer hidden states as memory and decodes them into KV caches, reporting a 1313× smaller memory state cache and 6.9× lower prefill latency for Qwen3.5-4B at 1M context.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27973v1.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28341v1.summary: Study of 2,100 fault-injected runs across four tool-using LLM agents finds recovery correct only 19-68% of the time, with 6-26% ending in confident fabrication, and a verification-first monitor cuts fabrication from 17.3% to 10.8%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28341v1.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28345v1.summary: Introduces two attacks on latent dynamic world models, state hallucination and dynamic shift, and finds that robust latent encoders are key, with adversarial encoder training improving robustness across four model families.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28345v1.title: Toward Adversarially Robust World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28349v1.summary: Introduces Grammar-as-a-Draft (GaaD), which merges grammar-forced tokens into speculative decoding draft rows for JSON, regex, and tool-call outputs, raising acceptance length and decoding speed in vLLM and Rust runtimes on TPU v7x.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28349v1.title: Grammar-as-a-Draft: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28454v1.summary: Proposes the Cumulative Consent Ledger, an approval interface that shows the cumulative consequences of an agent's action chain, and reports a study of 80 participants and a monitor that detected 89.2% of violating checkpoints.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28454v1.title: When a Permitted Action Completes a Forbidden Workflow: Designing Consequence-Oriented Approval for LLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28502v1.summary: Presents Shoonya, a family of from-scratch small language models (16.8M to 1.07B parameters) for Python, Rust and OpenCypher, paired with a pure-Rust runtime embedded directly in a graph database to avoid external model-server overhead.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28502v1.title: Shoonya: Zero-Socket In-Process Small Language Models for Graph Databases with Schema-Epoch KV Caching, Live Catalog Logit Masking, and Verifier-Advantage Distillation

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28522v1.summary: DisSparse integrates top-p sparse attention into vLLM, using a two-stream pipeline and histogram-based kernel to reduce block-selection latency, reporting 1.17x to 1.80x selection speedup and up to 8x larger batches.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28522v1.title: DisSparse: Pipelined Top-$p$ Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28558v1.summary: Proposes AOVO, a data-centric reinforcement learning framework that teaches multimodal LLMs when to use visual tools by reweighting training questions with perception attribution, without tool-specific rewards.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28558v1.title: From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28589v1.summary: CLOSE is a label-free verifier that uses a vision-language model's own yes/no object-presence judgments, with a rank-based threshold, to refuse hallucinated objects during generation, cutting CHAIRs on COCO for LLaVA-1.5-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28589v1.title: CLOSE: A Calibrated Label-free Online Self-Evaluating Verifier for Object Hallucination in Vision-Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28610v1.summary: Introduces a benchmark testing whether AI agents spend money well when buying information via USDC payments on Solana; three of 12 models passed 79 of 80 payment tasks, and estimated waste ranged from $21.0 to $70.8 per $100 spent.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28610v1.title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28655v1.title: UACR: Uncertainty-Aware Collaborative Routing for Explainable Industrial Anomaly Inspection

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28660v1.summary: Proposes a model-based insider attack in which a malicious agent in a multi-agent LLM debate or consensus game learns a world model of benign agents and a persuasion policy to degrade collective outcomes.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28660v1.title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28671v1.summary: Introduces MASSys, a benchmark that runs the same multi-agent LLM workflows across different serving substrates and load levels, showing that rankings such as Star versus Chain shift with KV-cache pressure.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28671v1.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28787v1.summary: DiscernBench is a benchmark of incident-report-based scenarios that tests whether LLM agents comply, refuse, or escalate in institutional settings; it finds role-specialized multi-agent deliberation raises average over-escalation from 3.79% to 28.27%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28787v1.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28947v1.summary: NightWatch is a plug-and-play framework pairing a computer-use VLM agent with a 0.8B-parameter monitoring model that streams interface state, cutting non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% on OSWorld and lifting DynaCU-Bench success from 39.5% to 44.2%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28947v1.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29014v1.summary: Introduces Population-Based Post-Training (PBPT), which trains several RLVR models in parallel and uses population-based training to tune hyperparameters, reporting stronger agents than compute-matched independent runs on four benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29014v1.title: Population-Based Post-Training for Large Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29242v1.summary: Studies coding-agent trajectories on DeepSWE, SWE-bench Verified and FeatureBench, finding that agents often leave consumer code defects after edits that original benchmark tests fail to detect.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29242v1.title: Edit-Induced Dependency Mismatch: Propagation Omissions, Recovery, and Evaluation Blind Spots in Coding Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29519v1.summary: Proposes an agent harness exposing intermediate model states and layer-level execution controls, with a prototype that chooses continue, exit, or stitch during inference; preliminary results report about 15% lower mean latency.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29519v1.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29590v1.summary: KernelShift is a benchmark that tests coding agents on CPU kernel optimization across Arm Neon, SVE, SVE2 and SME2, finding agents beat the compiler and some libraries but lag KleidiAI and struggle with SME2.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29590v1.title: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29663v1.summary: Examines whether LLM serving optimizations such as prefix caching, chunked prefill and speculative decoding, which are documented as exact, change individual graded answers even when aggregate benchmark accuracy stays the same.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29663v1.title: Exact on Paper: Which LLM Serving Shortcuts Flip Graded Answers, Measured Against the Noise of Reordering the Same Requests

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29679v1.summary: Proposes MERIT, a memory-augmented method for multi-session persuasive dialogue that uses persona-specific strategy records without parameter updates, and introduces the PERSIST dataset of 60 insurance-renewal personas over 10+ years.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29679v1.title: MERIT: Experience-Guided Memory for Long-Horizon Persona-Specific Persuasive Dialogue

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29697v1.summary: A protocol splits evidence-grounded fact-checking errors into retrieval, search control, judgement and verdict validation, finding that a single hybrid retrieval pass recovers complete evidence for 226 of 228 claims.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29697v1.title: Where Do Fact-Checking Errors Arise? Separating Retrieval, Search Control and Judgement in Evidence-Grounded Verification

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29734v1.summary: Proposes a training-free method that uses SVD to find the malicious subspace in latent activations and projects it out at inference, reducing backdoor attack success to an average of 2.07% across five CNN and ViT models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29734v1.title: Lightweight Spectral Subspace Filtering for Trojan-Resilient AI Inference Engines

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29773v1.summary: Introduces S1Arena-MM, a benchmark of 51,060 multimodal questions across 94 tasks and 102 game environments that compares 12 System-1 probability models with 21 MLLMs on the same decision requests.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29773v1.title: S1Arena-MM: Which Multimodal Decisions Can Be Left to System 1?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29909v1.summary: A survey of 116 works on inference-time methods for reducing LLM hallucination, comparing intervention families by evidence source, model access, and preparation cost, and noting metrics and limits to reported gains.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29909v1.title: Training-Free Interventions for Hallucination in Large Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29954v1.summary: Introduces Yggdrasil, a recurrent architecture that routes each layer's transition through a tree-indexed bank of experts, reporting it solves all five state-tracking tasks and runs faster on CPU than streaming baselines.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29954v1.title: Yggdrasil: Tree-Routed Recurrent Experts for State Tracking and Fast CPU Inference

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29977v1.summary: Introduces Conartist, a two-stage adaptive prompt injection framework that reports 32.12% attack success on a 576-instance tool-use benchmark and 66.67% on a Reddit GUI benchmark across five backbone models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29977v1.title: Conartist: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Computer-Using Agents against Multi-Step Prompt Injection

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29999v1.summary: Antiphony is a video deepfake detector that fuses four visual experts with thresholds calibrated on authentic videos and adds a tool-using multimodal investigator; it reports a mean benchmark score of 88.3% across six protocols.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29999v1.title: Antiphony: A Dual-Process Agent for Deepfake Video Detection with Real-Video Calibration

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30090v1.summary: Reports post-training an open-weight model, Kimi-K2.7, on 1,465 expert-authored long-document tasks, raising strict pass on a 100-task holdout from 11.0% to 24.5% without longer outputs.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30090v1.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30168v1.summary: Proposes FiRE, a reference-free machine translation evaluation method that uses off-the-shelf LLMs for criterion-driven pairwise comparisons on faithfulness, fluency, and style consistency, and releases a new human-annotated benchmark for it.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30168v1.title: FiRE: Fine-grained Ranking Evaluation for Machine Translation

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30202v1.summary: Introduces VADE, a data engine that builds verifiable open-ended analysis tasks from public professional sources; expert review of 186 finance tasks found 93.5% met a high bar, and training on them improved held-out and Finance Agent Benchmark v2 results.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30202v1.title: VADE: A Verifiable Agent Data Engine from Professional Sources

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30230v1.summary: Independently distilled 3B memory-writing and retrieval policies, combined with a fixed answer generator without joint training, reach 73.1% on a LongMemEval-based benchmark versus 36.2% for existing RL-trained specialists.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30230v1.title: Composing Independently Distilled Memory and Retrieval Policies for Long-Term Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30259v1.summary: Introduces TARE, a framework that attributes reported attack-success effects to the agent, attack, or defense only when they exceed the influence of content-free run state, such as hash seed and tool order, shown on the Agent Security Bench.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30259v1.title: Attributing Security Outcomes in LLM-Agent Evaluations: The Role of Content-Free State

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30365v1.summary: Presents mini-psych-agent, which converts psychological tasks into interactive environments and uses a learned human-policy model to measure how closely LLM agents' behavior matches human choices, finding this varies with agent configuration and task.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30365v1.title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30399v1.summary: Proposes cost-sensitive reversibility for non-deterministic actions, defining weak and strong reversal budgets and a reversibility lattice, with algorithms for computing budgets and rejecting bounded reversibility.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30399v1.title: Cost-Sensitive Reversibility of Non-Deterministic Actions

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30460v1.summary: Introduces CONCOR, a controlled benchmark that scores how contrastive decoding methods rank ground-truth objects against hallucinated candidates in multimodal LLMs, using a Contrastive Grounding Margin metric.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30460v1.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Contrastive Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30480v1.summary: Proposes Lobals, a training-free decoding method that re-runs a contiguous window of MLLM layers with the strongest visual-token attention to revisit visual evidence, reporting gains on vision-language, hallucination, and vision-centric tasks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30480v1.title: Test-Time Latent Computation to Improve Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30559v1.summary: Proposes State-Verified Reinforcement Learning, which trains tutoring agents using a deterministic verifier of workspace state changes; after training, Qwen3.8-27B's strict success on a 60-task benchmark rises from 51.47% to 80.74%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30559v1.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30690v1.summary: Proposes Attention-Patching, an implicit in-context learning method that fits layer-wise affine updates to attention output projections so it matches explicit ICL on 12 classification benchmarks at near zero-shot cost.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30690v1.title: Learn the Effects, Not the Examples: Implicit ICL via Attention Patching

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30702v1.summary: Study of empathetic RL against simulated users finds that raising the share of validation-seeking users makes the policy lower its bar for endorsing at-fault posters, with an explicit honesty request giving little protection.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30702v1.title: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30727v1.summary: CocoonBench is a benchmark of multilingual search tasks, rendered in three languages, that tests whether agents can find cross-lingual evidence; across 10 models, mean accuracy ranges from 33.8% to 69.7%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30727v1.title: CocoonBench: Can Multilingual Search Agents Escape Language Information Cocoons?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30742v1.summary: The paper shows that a single LLM-judge error correction can bias agent success rankings when judge errors depend on trajectories, and proposes AIPW with audit sampling that keeps bias and coverage errors small on a semi-synthetic benchmark.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30742v1.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30745v1.summary: Introduces IntentFlow, a mediation layer that checks tool-call arguments against a user intent contract and provenance policy; on a synthetic benchmark it cut attack success from 50.5% to 12.0%, with no benign tasks wrongly blocked.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30745v1.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30750v1.summary: Proposes a re-approval rule for AI agent tools that flags schema updates widening authority, with a Coq proof, 48 regression tests, and a pilot finding 412 of 580 compatible MCP schema changes silently widen some coordinate.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30750v1.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30771v1.summary: GameDojo is a benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 video games for testing real-time interactive agents, with coding agents building environments and gameplay scripts that produced 600 hours of trajectories.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30771v1.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30773v1.summary: Trallie is an open-source framework that uses LLMs for zero- or few-shot information extraction from HTML, PDF, TXT and JSON, and reportedly outperforms prior systems when target attributes are given.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30773v1.title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30825v1.summary: Analyzes Doc-to-LoRA, which compiles documents into low-rank adapters, finding it loses accuracy versus in-context learning on Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B, with multi-document interference and limited token savings.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30825v1.title: Doc-to-LoRA Analysis: Query Conditioning, Wrong Facts, and Distractor Interference

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30925v1.summary: PRIMEAPE is a multilingual benchmark of 2,205 response pairs across seven languages, with 11k human preference and rationale annotations, used to test whether LLM judges agree with human judgments.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30925v1.title: PRIMEAPE: A Multilingual Benchmark for Fine-Grained Meta-Evaluation of Judge Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30934v1.summary: LimeTree is a linear-complexity sequence model that adds synthetic key-value retrieval to language-model training, reporting WikiText-103 perplexity of 19 with 100% KV retrieval accuracy at a 16,384-token evaluation length.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30934v1.title: LimeTree: Linear-Memory Graph Neural Networks over Tree-Graphs for Resource-Efficient Language Modeling and Context Extrapolation

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30957v1.summary: SayDo benchmarks six VLMs across 11,480 episodes in eleven tasks, finding hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in simulated closed-loop robot control.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30957v1.title: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30965v1.summary: Proposes TT-RSI, a label-free test-time framework that re-solves questions using earlier solutions as references and distills refinements into model weights, reporting a +13.89% average accuracy gain over the base model.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30965v1.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30986v1.summary: Proposes iTDM, a method for aligning diffusion models with reward signals that addresses training instability from behavior-policy mismatch, reporting faster convergence on the GenEval2 benchmark.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30986v1.title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31002v1.summary: Introduces 10,807 resettable physics environments built from real-world videos, plus a 500-task zero-shot benchmark where frontier models reach 85.8% success versus 2.6% to 10.0% for open-source baselines.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31002v1.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31021v1.summary: LatentParse is a training-free framework that uses an analyst VLM to parse CLIP, DINOv3 and VGGT features into a text report of spatial evidence, improving five VLMs by 0.7-2.4 points on three spatial benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31021v1.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31027v1.summary: Introduces ComputeWise, an open benchmark and simulated GPU for measuring wasted GPU time by AI research agents; unaided agents spent 52% of GPU time on needed work, and an open-source harness removed over 80% of extra time across five models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31027v1.title: ComputeWise: Measuring and Fixing GPU Waste by AI Research Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31056v1.summary: DKnown-Jev-2 is an article-level classifier that labels whether a candidate article holds answer evidence for a normative question, reporting 91.77% accuracy and 91.28% macro-F1 on a 972-instance test set, 2.16 and 2.37 points above Jev.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31056v1.title: DKnown-Jev-2: Article-Level Answer-Evidence Classification and Efficient Inference with a Pre-trained Language Model

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31063v1.summary: Introduces REPA, a structural model that links measured local agent responses to system-level error propagation in LLM multi-agent workflows, evaluated on ErrPropBench-10 with three Qwen base models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31063v1.title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31089v1.title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31094v1.summary: LoopRes is a method that lets looped layers in pretrained LLMs attend to outputs of earlier loops using trainable loop-aware keys and a window of recent loops, reporting a 29.1% gain over SFT for Qwen3-1.7B-Base at 2x compute.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31094v1.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31099v1.summary: NoveltyGate is a training-free method that speeds up the π0.5 vision-language-action model's prefix by up to 1.61× on LIBERO by routing tokens to a low-rank or original MLP based on whether their inputs are novel.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31099v1.title: NoveltyGate: Novelty, Not Error, Decides Which VLA Prefix Tokens to Compute Exactly

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31101v1.summary: SayWhen is a test-time controller for voice agents that decides when to release speech before the user finishes, blocking playback if later transcripts invalidate the candidate; tested on a branching diagnostic and a 30-task simulation.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31101v1.title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31105v1.summary: LiveLoRA is a runtime method that migrates a session's final-block KV cache to a new LoRA adapter version without full-history re-prefill, reporting about 69x median speedup on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with 32 sessions of 8K tokens.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31105v1.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31110v1.summary: Preflight is a program-scoped verifier for Python dependencies that synthesizes function-level harnesses and runs them in a restricted environment, flagging malicious behavior in four incident contexts and clean verdicts on 100 benign packages.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31110v1.title: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31112v1.summary: Introduces Corrective Prefix Attention, a parallel speculative decoding method that lets draft tokens attend to earlier choices in the block, reporting 13–15% more committed tokens per round than DSpark and up to 3.37× mean speedup on Qwen3 targets.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31112v1.title: Look Back, Draft Ahead: Corrective Prefix Attention for Parallel Speculative Decoding

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31113v1.summary: Shows that zero-shot context-extension comparisons at default attention temperature are confounded by baseline miscalibration, which pure-bf16 training without master weights makes several times larger.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31113v1.title: Attention Temperature Confounds Zero-Shot Context Extension

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31115v1.summary: Introduces RUIBench, a 30-task robot manipulation benchmark, and RUIKit, a framework of 13 action interfaces; in simulation, changing only the interface raised a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31115v1.title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31117v1.summary: A 27B language-model embodied agent in a household environment edits one tensor of its own weights overnight, tested against its unchanged self, and the kept edit improves task completion and step efficiency.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31117v1.title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31129v1.summary: Presents FATCAT, a non-invasive electromagnetic fault-injection attack on GPU-based SoCs that uses an RF side-channel trigger to make Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B fulfill refused requests, and shows it can drive a robotic arm into hazardous motions.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31129v1.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31154v1.summary: Proposes Attention Latent Feedback, which lets each sublayer attend to deeper-layer outputs at the previous token; on MoE models up to 4.0B parameters it lowers held-out loss by 0.022-0.024 nats for about 1.1% extra decoding FLOPs.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31154v1.title: Attention Latent Feedback

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31160v1.summary: Introduces Habitats, a framework that evolves populations of reward-policy pairs using a Planner that directs a separate Mutator to write reward programs, tested on a Card Sandbox and three control tasks against two baselines.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31160v1.title: Habitats: A Framework for Open-Ended Evolution of Agent Objectives

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31163v1.summary: SPROUT is a prompt-selection method for preference tuning of text-to-image diffusion models that predicts each prompt's gradient-norm utility with a text-only model and reaches uniform sampling's final GenEval score in about 44% of iterations.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31163v1.title: SPROUT: Predicting Objective-Grounded Prompt Utility for Efficient Text-to-Image Preference Tuning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31164v1.summary: Proposes two guidance mechanisms, anti-drifting and motion-aware guidance, for distilling autoregressive video models with FlowMap methods; 4-step π-Flow students match DMD students from 14B teachers on VBench.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31164v1.title: Analyzing and Improving FlowMap Distillation of Autoregressive Video Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31166v1.summary: Proposes TipSweep, which searches the learning rate by training only the last block(s) of an LLM and predicts the optimal rate for full-depth post-training, with the scaling exponent depending on FP32 or BF16 weight precision.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31166v1.title: Precision-Aware Learning Rate Transfer Across Block Count in LLM Post-Training

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31174v1.summary: Across ten decision models, the paper finds that the order in which options are presented substantially degrades accuracy, then compares eight mitigation methods and reports tree attention as effective, with a 1.1-point accuracy drop.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31174v1.title: Reducing Order Sensitivity in Decision Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31185v1.summary: CO-GRAFT is a framework that attributes RL gains in Search-R1 search agents to four functional roles by mixing RL-trained and pre-RL policies, finding query generation contributes at most 15% of the gain.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31185v1.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31198v1.summary: Introduces ToolSmith, a framework that automatically generates and reuses new tools on top of a lean base library for multimodal search agents, evaluated on 13 benchmarks with gains that grow with backbone size.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31198v1.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31215v1.summary: ActSpace-Bench is a benchmark of 994 spatial questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, testing whether VLMs actively seek evidence before answering; strongest models explore purposefully but lose evidence to limited memory.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31215v1.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31223v1.summary: Proposes a three-agent framework (language-model interpreter, Bayesian optimizer, multi-objective reinforcement learning controller) that links high-level network intents to runtime radio resource control, tested in a differentiated connectivity case study.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31223v1.title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31228v1.summary: Four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Phi-4) fail to verbalize lower confidence at their own math reasoning errors, but do correct more when an injected low-confidence tag is added.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31228v1.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31233v1.summary: TowerBridge is a closed-form weight-editing recipe for CLIP-style dual encoders that attenuates directions where the image and text towers agree on hard negatives, raising COCO and Flickr30k retrieval across 21 checkpoints.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31233v1.title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31338v1.summary: Argues that per-attack blocking misleads for agent tool manifests and reports synthetic, author-pilot, and real MCP-tool results showing catalogs with many tools are far more often vulnerable than per-attack rates suggest.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31338v1.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31346v1.summary: Introduces InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark that labels six fine-grained information manipulation strategies in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, and fabrication, plus a coarse consistency label, and benchmarks representative multimodal models on it.
